original.question: According to the course (Java 8-era interfaces): State the difference between an abstract class and an interface for (1) variables, (2) constructors and (3) methods, and say which one to use for unrelated classes.
original.answer:
(1) Abstract class: no restrictions on variables; interface: variables must be public static final.
(2) Abstract class: constructors are invoked by subclasses through constructor chaining; interface: no constructors. Neither can be created with new.
(3) Abstract class: no restrictions on methods (abstract methods cannot be static); interface: methods must be public abstract.
Use an interface to give common behavior to unrelated classes; an abstract class models common behavior of related classes.

versions.question: According to the course (Java 8-era interfaces): Complete the comparison. For an interface: variables are ____, constructors are ____, methods are ____. For an abstract class the three are: ____, ____ and ____.
versions.answer:
Interface: variables public static final; no constructors; methods public abstract.
Abstract class: no restrictions on variables; constructors invoked by subclasses through constructor chaining; no restrictions on methods (abstract methods cannot be static).
Neither can be instantiated with new.

versions.question: Give one example of two unrelated classes that share a behavior, and show which construct models it and how a class joins it.
versions.answer: Apple (extends Fruit) and Chicken (extends Animal) are both edible. Define `public interface Edible { String howToEat(); }`, and let each class declare `implements Edible` with a public howToEat(). An abstract class cannot do this because the classes already have different superclasses.
